short: Giving each user only the access their job requires.
seoTitle: Role-Based Access — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: Giving each user only the access their job requires. Each user logs in as themselves. Shared logins destroy accountability.
definition: Role-based access assigns permissions by role rather than by person — a cashier bills, a manager approves discounts and voids, an owner sees reports and settings. Each user logs in as themselves.
bodyHtml:
Why Role-Based Access matters

Shared logins destroy accountability. Without individual users, no void, discount or price override can be traced to anyone, and the audit trail becomes decorative.

How Role-Based Access works in practice

Give each person their own login, restrict discounts, voids and price edits to supervisors, and review those actions weekly. Remove access the same day someone leaves.

faq.question: Why not use one shared login for the counter?
faq.answer: Because every action then belongs to everybody, and no discrepancy can be traced.

faq.question: Which actions should require approval?
faq.answer: Discounts, voids after printing, price overrides and back-dated entries.
